newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended off session peaks, as the long end of the yield curve proved sensitive to EMU jitters and became depressed by a fall seen in the Italian Btp market.

"We are going through a normal consolidation process ahead of Thursday's CPI," said Gregorio Gomez at All Trading in Madrid. He said the Spanish market would probably stay in a tight range on Wednesday, before announcement of January inflation.
But Bonos remained well positioned against the German market as the 10-year spread over Bunds fell to 116 basis points from 127 bps this morning.
January CPI is expected to have increased month-on-month at around 0.4 percent and 3.0 percent year-on-year.
"But I do not expect the Bank of Spain will cut rates, even with data better than that," said Gomez.

Salomon Brothers in London, which forecasts CPI to rise 3.0 percent with the core index up 2.8 pct, is ruling out a quick move by the Bank of Spain. They are expecting a 25 bp reduction in the repo rate after February CPI and before the end of March.
"It would be difficult to see a cut in the official rate, after the peseta's recent volatility," said another analyst.
